body:
Machine safety: processes, the live server and store, git and Windows traps. (Revision 6, Termal::Architect1 on 2026-10-08 for w-300e42c8f565: the archive target of worktree removal is now the main checkout's Git-ignored .evidence/, per CLAUDE.md "Work only in the repository folder" as landed in e35a31d2; revision 5 condensed revision 4's worktree sections into one ordered procedure; history is in earlier revisions.)

PROCESSES (Termal::Fable2, 2026-09-30)
- Agents do not end processes by hand: no Stop-Process, taskkill, kill or process-tree termination. To stop your own background run, use the runtime's own stop. If a launcher or stage survives, let it end, then settle it with `node scripts/test-launcher.mjs recover RUN_DIRECTORY`.
- If a process truly must end, report it to the coordinator with its PID, command line, working or run directory and start time. The coordinator decides, and asks Greg where it is not provably the requester's own.
- A launcher's command line identifies nothing, and Windows reuses PIDs. Only the working or run directory plus the start time ties a process to a run (w-a04cdfa3e63f).
- Do not stop a running gate to change its input. Never touch another project's processes.
- Crossed "wait" (#1158): when a launch crosses a hold, let the run finish and report; never end it, not even your own launcher.

LIVE SERVER AND STORE
- Greg starts TermAl with `cargo run --release` in the master checkout; that long-lived cargo.exe is the live server's parent. Never end it, and never count it as a gate. `cargo build --release` in master fails with os error 5 while it runs.
- Never run sqlite3 or any tool that opens ~/.termal/termal.sqlite, even read-only; it killed the running TermAl once. Use the HTTP API, open it only while TermAl is stopped, or ask Greg for an export.
- /api/state returns summary-only sessions (messages:[], messagesLoaded:false; real size is messageCount), and it does not expose ignoredDiscoveredCodexThreadIds. Never infer absence from a field not proven populated; cross-check before any destructive action.

GIT ON THIS MACHINE
- `git apply --3way --check` is not a dry run (it rewrites the index). Use plain `git apply --check`; after a deliberate 3-way, `git reset -- <files>`.
- `git apply` inside an export under target/ discovers the enclosing repo and silently ignores outside paths. Use GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES=/c/github/Personal/TermAl/target, then prove the patch landed.
- Git against a nested scratch repo can act on master (Opus2, 2026-10-01: a half-created probe committed master's index). Never run git against a possibly unreadable nested repo; if needed, set GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES and explicit --git-dir/--work-tree.
- Hand-back fingerprints: `git diff HEAD -- <files> | sha256sum` in Git for Windows bash. Codex calls `C:/Program Files/Git/bin/bash.exe -lc`, because a bare bash resolves to WSL git, which sees CRLF differently.
- Right after a merge or HEAD move, freeze components can read wrong: run `git update-index --refresh`, and rewrite auto-merged paths from the index (w-0c021ce2b34a).

LINE ENDINGS AND FORMATTING
- msys grep and sed strip CR before matching. Use `git ls-files --eol`, perl, or `tr -cd '\r' | wc -c`.
- The index is LF and core.autocrlf=true; the hazard is a surviving `\r\r\n`. Check with `git diff | perl -ne 'print if /^\+.*\r/'`.
- `sed -i` rewrites CRLF files as LF; use the Edit tool. src/*.rs are include! fragments, so judge formatting only with `cargo fmt -- --check`.

WORKTREE REMOVAL: ONE ORDERED PROCEDURE (incidents: master's node_modules was deleted through a junction at 08:38Z on 2026-10-06, note 78d03cb6; gate logs were lost at 22:05Z on 2026-10-05 and again at about 09:50-11:50Z on 2026-10-06 for test-6c62b096, test-8a57d2b1 and test-eff26db9, note bb03aa2a; all on w-4f266a83379d). Launcher logs live in .git/worktrees/<wt>/review-runs, outside the worktree, and `git worktree remove` deletes them. Gate worktrees may hold ui\node_modules as a JUNCTION to master's, and a recursive delete or worktree remove follows it into master. For EVERY removal, in this order:
1. ARCHIVE: copy .git/worktrees/<wt>/review-runs to the main checkout's .evidence/<wt>/ (C:\github\Personal\TermAl\.evidence\<wt>\, Git-ignored), and verify the file count and hashes. Never to .tmp/review-runs-archive/ (retired on 2026-10-08 by w-300e42c8f565: its open-task runs were moved to .evidence/, the rest listed and removed) and never outside the repository. A run archived there is an artifact of the task it served: it is removed when every task it serves has closed, unless an open task records a concrete need and when it ends (CLAUDE.md "Work only in the repository folder"); the agent that closes the last such task, or the coordinator's sweep, removes it after the path check and records what it removed. Quote in Engram what a decision rests on; the raw file is not the lasting record.
2. JUNCTION: unlink ui\node_modules itself (`cmd /c rmdir` or fs.unlink), verify it is gone as a reparse point, and STOP if that fails.
3. INTEGRITY: verify master's ui/node_modules against ui/package-lock.json (non-optional entries present, .bin exists), never by counting entries.
4. REMOVE: `git worktree remove`, without --force unless the worktree is verified clean.
Repair a damaged node_modules with `npm ci` in master ui/ while no UI test is running; if a dev server locks esbuild, use `npm install --no-save` plus `npm rebuild --ignore-scripts`. A shared node_modules is no reason to serialise gates. Coordinators put all four steps in every cleanup instruction.
Before any recursive delete under .evidence/ or .tmp/: resolve the absolute path, assert it lies under C:\github\Personal\TermAl\, and assert that neither the target nor anything under it is a reparse point (a `Get-ChildItem -Recurse -Force` filtered on ReparsePoint); stop and report if one is found. A shell whose cwd is inside the target makes Move-Item/Remove-Item fail with "in use": cd out first.

PLAINLY (revision 7, Termal::Architect1, 2026-10-08, at Fable2's request #544): from 2026-10-06 (CLAUDE.md as landed in e35a31d2) a worktree's review-runs are archived ONLY to C:\github\Personal\TermAl\.evidence\<wt>\. .tmp\review-runs-archive\ is retired: w-300e42c8f565 moved its open-task runs to .evidence/ and removed the rest on 2026-10-08. Two archives (wt-workspace-lookups-11336, wt-workspace-lookups-integrated-11336) were still put under .tmp\review-runs-archive\ on 2026-10-07, so not every session knows this yet: check this entry and CLAUDE.md "Work only in the repository folder" before archiving, and do not create .tmp\review-runs-archive\ again; anything left there goes to the coordinator's sweep.

ADDENDUM (Termal::Fable2, 2026-10-08, w-d0b43b44082d): a worktree's ui\node_modules may be a REAL directory whose CHILDREN are junctions into master's node_modules. TermAl-wt-winf-r6 held 288 such per-package junctions, and a check of only the top-level node_modules would have missed them. Before any removal, scan the WHOLE worktree with `Get-ChildItem -Recurse -Force -Attributes ReparsePoint`, validate every hit (type, target, parent), unlink each with a non-recursive [IO.Directory]::Delete(path, $false), re-scan to 0, and only then remove the worktree.

CRLF ON CARRY (Opus3, 2026-10-19, w-6c3e): `git -c core.autocrlf=false merge --ff-only` still wrote CRLF into 23 clean files. Run every carry step under `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=core.autocrlf GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=false`. To repair clean files: rm, then checkout under it. Verify with `ls-files --eol | grep -c w/crlf` = 0; freeze fingerprints don't catch it.
